title: „První Evropané“ byli kanibalové, ale nejedli jen děti, naznačuje výzkum
content:
Nové archeologické objevy ve Španělsku prokázaly, že první zástupci rodu Homo, kteří osídlili Evropu, sice byli kanibalové, ale ne kanibalové, kteří by konzumovali jenom dětské maso.
Homo antecessor by se dal s nadsázkou označit za „prvního Evropana“. Šlo totiž zřejmě o jeden z prvních druhů zástupc
label: adverse
max_acceptable_basis: p90 of 2091 scored cultural_discovery articles in filtered_20260801_165523 (median 1.0802, p99 4.9205, max 7.2077)
why_adverse: A real archaeological finding, and that is what makes it hard: the Atapuerca dig, the 24 Homo antecessor individuals and the challenge to the 2011 exocannibalism hypothesis are all genuine discovery, and discovery_novelty 7.10 / evidence_quality 7.26 are honest readings of the text. What the lens has no dimension for is what the finding is OF. The news hook is not "new site transforms what we know about the first Europeans" — it is that the cannibalism was not confined to children, i.e. the harm detail IS the news, carried in the headline. Scored raw 6.14 against a batch p99 of 4.92, so it did not merely enter the lens, it topped it. Discovery is meant to surface knowledge that adds to a living world; a maximally-ranked headline about prehistoric humans butchering children and adults is the boundary this case marks. Adjacent to the historical_harm_reckoning bucket from the v5 hard-negative cohort (#62), but distinct: there is no modern community, no moral reckoning, and no perpetrator — only subject matter.
misleading_features: strong archaeological-discovery vocabulary (site, remains, stone tools, dating)
a named institution and a dated, citable study
an explicit hypothesis-overturned frame ("bod zlomu" / turning point)
forward-looking research agenda in the closing paragraphs
high evidence quality — the article is well-sourced, which the lens rewards directly

title: Pocken: Europäer brachten einst die Pocken nach Amerika
content:
Genanalyse an Mumien Europäer brachten einst die Pocken nach Amerika
Die Europäer waren es: Durch Analysen von Pocken-Erbgut aus Mumien in Chile hat ein internationales Forschungsteam den bislang eindeutigsten Beweis dafür geliefert, dass die auch in Amerika verheerende Krankheit aus Europa stammte.
label: adverse
max_acceptable_basis: p90 of 2312 scored cultural_discovery articles in filtered_20260804_045930 (median 1.0717, p99 4.9118)
why_adverse: The finding is real and the scoring is honest, which is what makes this the harder half of the class. The first smallpox genomes recovered from the Americas, from two mummified individuals buried in northern Chile between the late 15th and early 17th centuries, settle a long-running question about colonial-era introduction. evidence_quality 8.00 and discovery_novelty 7.10 are correct readings of a rigorously sourced piece reporting a genuine methodological first — and "a loop closes, knowledge accumulates" is normally qualifying for this lens. What decides it is the difference between what underpins the story and what the story is about. The genomics is the instrument; the subject is that Europeans brought the disease that devastated the Americas, and that is what a reader carries away. Discovery exists to correct declinism and presentism — the past proving nearer, more capable, or something lost restored. Establishing that a colonial harm occurred does none of those, and the lens has no dimension that asks what the finding is OF. Scored raw 6.5582 against a batch p99 of 4.9118: it topped the lens rather than merely entering it. Same class as czech_ct24_3c8799a303a0 (Atapuerca cannibalism), but distinguishable from it by carrying a real achievement underneath — a v6 hard-negative cohort should not learn from this that ancient-genomics reporting is adverse per se.
misleading_features: first-of-its-kind framing ("first molecular evidence") that reads directly as discovery_novelty
named researcher and institution (Trinity College Dublin) with a dated, citable study
ancient-DNA methodology vocabulary — genomes, mummified remains, a radiocarbon-bounded window
maximal evidence_quality: the piece is rigorously sourced, which the lens rewards directly
a long-standing scientific debate presented as settled, which reads as knowledge accumulating

title: Momias incas de hace 500 años encontradas en Chile demuestran que los colonizadores europeos llevaron la viruela a América
content:
Momias incas de hace 500 años encontradas en Chile demuestran que los colonizadores europeos llevaron la viruela a América
Arqueología
La mujer y el joven estudiados murieron durante un brote que ocurrió entre 1492 y 1631 después de Cristo
Devastados por la enfermedad, dos cuerpos fueron envueltos e
label: adverse
max_acceptable_basis: p90 of 2225 scored cultural_discovery articles in filtered_20260804_005402 (median 1.0858, p99 5.1081)
why_adverse: The same study as german_spiegel_wissenschaft_4cfe2e08cd81, reported by a different outlet in a different language, scored in a different batch, and published to the Discovery feed on the same day — the reader flagged both within two minutes of each other. The rationale is identical: genuine ancient-genomics work on two 500-year-old Inca mummies, honestly scored (evidence_quality 8.00, discovery_novelty 7.33), where the subject of the finding is that European colonisers introduced smallpox to the Americas. The recovered knowledge establishes a harm; it does not bring the past nearer, show it more capable, or restore anything lost. Scored raw 6.6737 against a batch p99 of 5.1081. Worth carrying into training as a PAIR rather than as two independent examples: they are one event, and their appearing separately in the same feed is also evidence of the cross-language dedup gap (NexusMind#291/#295), not only of a lens-fidelity gap.
misleading_features: archaeological-discovery vocabulary (mummies, remains, outbreak dating 1492-1631)
natural-mummification and preservation detail reading as evidence_quality
a named institution and a specific, checkable claim
colonial-contact framing that scores as cross_cultural_connection (5.86) — the dimension reads contact between cultures without regard to what the contact was
heritage_significance 7.10, identical to every other cultural_discovery case in this batch — worth checking for saturation independently of this row

title: VIDEO : Le dernier voyage sacrificiel de trois enfants incas
content: Des chercheurs ont réussi à reconstituer plusieurs mois de la vie de trois enfants sacrifiés durant un rituel inca il y a plus de 500 ans. Ce rituel, c’est la capacocha : un immense pèlerinage, parfois long de plusieurs milliers de kilomètres, qui traversait tout l'empire avant de s'achever au somme
label: adverse
max_acceptable_basis: p90 of 2225 scored cultural_discovery articles in filtered_20260804_005402 (median 1.0858, p99 5.1081)
why_adverse: The cleanest case in this batch, because there is no methodological first to weigh against the subject matter. Researchers reconstructed the final months of three children sacrificed in an Inca capacocha ritual over 500 years ago, tracing a pilgrimage to an Andean summit. The archaeology is genuine and evidence_quality 7.26 / discovery_novelty 7.10 are honest readings. The dimension to look at is human_resonance at 6.61 — the highest of the four cultural_discovery cases in this batch. What it is responding to is the death of three named children rendered as a narrative, and the lens has no way to tell 'humanly resonant' from 'humanly distressing'. Nothing here reaches the present: no institution acting, no restitution, no capability recovered. The reconstruction establishes what was done to them and stops there. Scored raw 6.4432 against a batch p99 of 5.1081.
misleading_features: isotope and archaeological-science methodology applied to named individuals
a reconstructed narrative arc (a pilgrimage, the final months) that reads as human_resonance
cultural-practice framing (capacocha, the Inca empire, sacred mountaintops) reading as heritage_significance
high evidence quality on a well-documented excavation
video-feature packaging, which signals editorial investment rather than lens fit

title: Kixikila: uma forma de organização social e econômica em Angola
content:
Por Elisabete Vitorino*
Pensar na África e na diáspora negra africana é estabelecer conexões entre o Brasil, os países africanos e todos os outros territórios em que estão descendentes de africanos. As conexões são inúmeras e, nesta edição da coluna, iremos até Angola para conhecer uma forma de orga
label: adverse
max_acceptable_basis: p90 of 3463 scored cultural_discovery articles in filtered_20260805_051624 (median 1.0508, p99 4.0822)
why_adverse:
A different failure from the four cases already in this file. Those are "the harm is the finding" — the actors are dead and nothing carries forward. Here there is no finding at all. Kixikila is a rotating savings and credit association Angolans run today; the article is ethnographic description of a living practice. Nothing was recovered, nothing lost was restored, and the past is not shown to be nearer or more capable than assumed — the three ways ovr.news BRAND.md says a Discovery qualifies. The lens admitted it on topic proximity alone, which is the failure mode that criterion was written to exclude.

The scorer's own numbers say so. discovery_novelty (5.58) is the LOWEST of the five dimensions and the only one that encodes whether an epistemic event occurred; cross_cultural_connection (8.00) and heritage_significance (7.10) are the highest and both fire on subject matter. So the lens-defining dimension was outvoted 2:1 by topic-proximity dimensions. That makes this a weighting problem with a concrete target, unlike the smallpox and Inca rows where no dimension was wrong.

The correct destination is belonging ("living cultural practices and heritage"), which scored this 9.807 normalized against cultural_discovery's 9.850 — a margin of 0.043 decided the placement. So the fix has unusual leverage: a small correction on the discovery side moves the article into the right lens rather than out of the feed. Do not use this row to teach suppression of African or non-Western traditional practice — the article is good and belongs on the site, in a different lens.

The reader asked why it was not a solution. It is a defensible reading (our own summary calls Kixikila "a social technology"), but the solutions scorer never scored this article at all — there is no row for it in ovr.news article_filter_scores — so solutions was never in the contest. Belonging was, and lost by 0.04.
misleading_features: cross_cultural_connection 8.00, the top dimension: a non-Western communal practice explained to an outside audience scores cultural distance, which measures the reader's unfamiliarity, not whether anything was discovered
heritage_significance 7.10: the practice genuinely is heritage, but LIVING heritage — the dimension does not distinguish a practice still in daily use from one that was recovered
Academic framing (a named researcher, "ongoing research", a comparison to Brazil's Banco Palmas) reads as a study reporting a finding, when the research is description of a current practice
Kimbundu etymology and origin-of-the-practice framing supply past-tense vocabulary with no past-tense claim attached

heritage_significance is 7.10 here and on three of the four earlier cultural_discovery cases (all but Atapuerca, which is 6.40). Kixikila is the first of those four that shares no subject matter with the others, which is why it is evidence for saturation rather than for a subject cluster — see llm-distillery#87 and the 2026-08-05 adjudication note
